_source_note: A reference set describing each state's Department of Insurance (DOI) complaint process and independent external review framework in general, plain-language terms. Regulator names and well-documented program names (e.g. California's Independent Medical Review, North Carolina's Smart NC) are real and were checked during development; exact statute numbers are deliberately NOT cited per-state because those change and were not individually verified - the one citation used throughout is the genuine, stable federal baseline: 45 CFR 147.136 (the ACA's internal claims/appeals and external review regulation). Contact details are given as instructions for where to find current, official info (a search term or a stable federal directory URL), never as a specific phone number, which goes stale and cannot be verified offline. This is not legal advice. Covers a sample of 10 states plus DEFAULT (the federal fallback used for any other state, or when the patient's state can't be determined).

CA.doi_name: California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) for most HMO plans, or the California Department of Insurance (CDI) for most PPO/indemnity plans
CA.doi_complaint_process: Both regulators accept consumer complaints about how an insurer handled a claim (delays, failure to follow required procedures, etc.), separate from the medical necessity decision itself. DMHC's Help Center and CDI's Consumer Hotline both take complaints online or by phone.
CA.external_review_process: California's independent external review is commonly known as Independent Medical Review (IMR) for DMHC-regulated plans, or a similar independent review process for CDI-regulated plans - a doctor with no stake in the outcome reviews the denial.
CA.external_review_deadline_window: Your plan's final internal appeal denial letter states the exact deadline to request review. If that's unclear, the federal minimum floor of at least 4 months (120 days) after the final internal denial still applies (45 CFR 147.136).
CA.doi_contact_instruction: Search 'California DMHC Help Center' (for HMO plans) or 'California Department of Insurance consumer complaint' (for PPO plans) for current phone numbers and online complaint forms - contact details change, so do not rely on a number from this file.
CA.regulatory_note: General ACA external review framework (45 CFR 147.136), implemented in California partly through the DMHC/CDI independent review programs described above.

NY.doi_name: New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS)
NY.doi_complaint_process: DFS accepts consumer complaints about how a health insurer handled a claim, including delays and failure to follow required procedures, through its online complaint portal.
NY.external_review_process: New York's external appeal process lets a patient request review by a DFS-certified independent review organization after exhausting the internal appeal (or in certain urgent situations without waiting).
NY.external_review_deadline_window: Check your internal appeal denial letter for the exact deadline; the federal minimum floor of at least 4 months (120 days) after the final internal denial applies (45 CFR 147.136).
NY.doi_contact_instruction: Search 'New York DFS health insurance complaint' or 'New York DFS external appeal' for current online complaint and external-appeal request forms - do not rely on a phone number from this file.
NY.regulatory_note: General ACA external review framework (45 CFR 147.136), implemented in New York through DFS's external appeal process.

TX.doi_complaint_process: TDI accepts consumer complaints about how an insurer handled a claim, including untimely responses and procedural failures, through its online complaint system.
TX.external_review_process: Texas uses independent review organizations (IROs) certified by TDI to conduct external reviews of denied claims involving medical judgment.
TX.external_review_deadline_window: Check your internal appeal denial letter for the exact deadline; the federal minimum floor of at least 4 months (120 days) after the final internal denial applies (45 CFR 147.136).
TX.doi_contact_instruction: Search 'Texas Department of Insurance file a complaint' or 'Texas TDI independent review organization' for current contact and request forms - do not rely on a phone number from this file.
TX.regulatory_note: General ACA external review framework (45 CFR 147.136), implemented in Texas through TDI's IRO program.

FL.doi_complaint_process: The Department of Financial Services' Division of Consumer Services accepts complaints about how a claim was handled, including delays and procedural failures.
FL.external_review_process: Florida-regulated plans provide access to an independent external review by a certified independent review organization after the internal appeal is exhausted.
FL.external_review_deadline_window: Check your internal appeal denial letter for the exact deadline; the federal minimum floor of at least 4 months (120 days) after the final internal denial applies (45 CFR 147.136).
FL.doi_contact_instruction: Search 'Florida Department of Financial Services insurance consumer complaint' for the current online complaint form and contact info - do not rely on a phone number from this file.
FL.regulatory_note: General ACA external review framework (45 CFR 147.136), implemented in Florida through the state's independent review process.

IL.regulatory_note: General ACA external review framework (45 CFR 147.136), implemented in Illinois through the state's independent review process.

NC.external_review_process: North Carolina provides an independent external review process for denials involving medical judgment, conducted by a certified independent review organization after the internal appeal is exhausted - Smart NC can help file the request.
NC.external_review_deadline_window: Check your internal appeal denial letter for the exact deadline; the federal minimum floor of at least 4 months (120 days) after the final internal denial applies (45 CFR 147.136).
NC.doi_contact_instruction: Search 'North Carolina Smart NC health insurance help' for current contact info and online complaint/external-review forms - do not rely on a phone number from this file.
NC.regulatory_note: General ACA external review framework (45 CFR 147.136), implemented in North Carolina through the Smart NC-assisted independent review process.

DEFAULT.state_name: your state (not in ClaimClarity's bundled sample, or not determined from the documents)
DEFAULT.doi_name: Your state Department of Insurance - or, if this is a self-funded employer plan governed by ERISA rather than a fully-insured plan, the U.S. Department of Labor's Employee Benefits Security Administration (EBSA)
DEFAULT.doi_complaint_process: Every state has a consumer complaint process for how an insurer handled a claim (delays, failure to follow required procedures, etc.), separate from the medical necessity decision itself. For a self-funded ERISA plan, that complaint instead goes to the DOL's EBSA rather than a state DOI.
DEFAULT.external_review_process: Under the ACA, your plan must offer independent external review for denials involving medical judgment or rescission - either through your state's own external review process, or through the HHS-administered Federal External Review Process, run by an independent third party with no stake in the outcome (45 CFR 147.136).
DEFAULT.external_review_deadline_window: At least 4 months (120 days) after you receive the final internal appeal denial, per the federal minimum standard (45 CFR 147.136) - your denial/appeal letter is legally required to state the exact deadline and process for your plan; use that date.
DEFAULT.doi_contact_instruction: Look up your state's Department of Insurance at the NAIC's official state insurance department directory (https://content.naic.org/state-insurance-departments), or, for a self-funded/ERISA plan, contact the DOL's EBSA at askebsa.dol.gov - do not rely on a phone number from this file, contact info changes.
DEFAULT.regulatory_note: General ACA external review framework (45 CFR 147.136). State-specific process details were not in ClaimClarity's bundled sample for this state - your denial notice's own external review instructions (required by law to be included) are the authoritative source.
